title: Construction of 14-metal lanthanide nanorings with NIR luminescence response to ions

synthesis.procedure: Under dry dinitrogen using standard Schlenk techniques, Nd(OAc)3·4H2O (0.40 mmol, 0.1573 g) and H2L (2,3-dihydroxybenzaldehyde, 0.60 mmol, 0.0829 g) were dissolved in 30 mL EtOH and 5 mL DMF at room temperature. A 10 mL EtOH solution of triethylamine (1.0 mol/L) was added. The mixture was stirred under reflux for 30 minutes and filtered. Red crystals formed after one week by slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate. The solid was dried at 120 °C for five hours.

synthesis.time: 30 min reflux; crystallization over one week; drying for 5 h
synthesis.vessel_or_method: Schlenk technique under dry dinitrogen; reflux; slow diffusion of diethyl ether
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered, then crystallized by slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the filtrate; solid dried in an oven at 120 °C for five hours.

properties.summary: 1 shows ligand-centered visible emission and Nd(III) NIR emission at 875, 1063 and 1337 nm from ligand-to-metal energy transfer. In CH3CN it acts as a reusable NIR luminescence sensor, with strong quenching by Cu(II), Co(II), H2PO4− and F−.
